title: Real-Time Image Analysis in Microscopy: A Reward-Based Workflow Approach
content: Real-time image analysis in STEM and AFM is essential for uncovering the physical and chemical properties of materials, enabling informed decision-making, and advancing experimental workflows [1, 2]. Automated imaging tools increasingly require unsupervised methods that optimize data representation for human interpretation or autonomous experimentation, as classical and neural network-based methods often depend on human input, such as hyperparameter tuning or data labelling [3]. Reward-based workflows address this challenge by framing image analysis as a decision-making process guided by reward functions, enabling robust, explainable, and adaptive optimization [4]. In this study, these workflows were applied to real-time STEM and AFM imaging, achieving effective segmentation, feature extraction, and clustering [5]. By leveraging human decision-making principles, the framework dynamically explores operational spaces, ensuring scalability, robustness, and explainability across a variety of imaging tasks.
